statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-8798 (GHSA-v6w3-qrh8-qccc): in Bouncy Castle for Java FIPS, the native entropy source used on Intel platforms retried the RDSEED and RDRAND instructions without limit, so a persistent failure of the CPU entropy source could hang any thread drawing from it inside the JNI call. bc-fips 2.1.0 to 2.1.2 are affected and 2.1.3 bounds the retries: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-v6w3-qrh8-qccc, https://github.com/bcgit/bc-java/wiki/CVE%E2%80%902026%E2%80%908798. The affected code is in the x86-64 Linux native libraries inside the bc-fips jar (native/linux/x86_64); the 2.1.3 libraries carry the new 'RDSEED persistently failed to produce entropy' and 'RDRAND persistently failed to produce entropy' errors, which the 2.1.2 libraries lack. Upstream lists only x86 and x86-64 with the native library in use as affected, so aarch64 builds do not run this code, but the range below covers the owner as a whole. The DHI eclipse-temurin-11-jre packages for Alpine 3.23 ship Bouncy Castle FIPS in their eclipse-temurin-11-jre-fips subpackage, as /usr/lib/bouncycastle/bc-fips-<version>.jar, byte-identical to the Maven Central bc-fips jar of that version. Read the bc-fips jar manifest in every published eclipse-temurin-11-jre-fips package for Alpine 3.23 (x86_64: 16 versions, 11.0.30.7-r0 to 11.0.33.10-r1; aarch64: 8 versions, 11.0.30.7-r0 to 11.0.31.11-r6); each download matched the repository index checksum. bc-fips is 2.1.2 in 11.0.30.7-r0 to 11.0.32.1.1-r0 and in 11.0.32.9-r0, and 2.1.3 in 11.0.32.1.1-r1 and in 11.0.32.9.1.1-r2 and every later build. Under apk version ordering 11.0.32.9-r0 sorts between 11.0.32.1.1-r1 and 11.0.32.9.1.1-r2, so the range has two spans: affected below 11.0.32.1.1-r1, fixed from 11.0.32.1.1-r1, affected again from 11.0.32.9-r0, and fixed from 11.0.32.9.1.1-r2.

CVE-2026-8798 (GHSA-v6w3-qrh8-qccc): in Bouncy Castle for Java FIPS (bc-fips) 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, the native entropy source used on x86 and x86-64 when the native library is in use (NativeEntropySource) retried the RDSEED and RDRAND instructions without a bound, so a persistent failure of those instructions could hang the calling thread; bc-fips 2.1.3 fixes it: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-v6w3-qrh8-qccc, https://github.com/bcgit/bc-java/wiki/CVE%E2%80%902026%E2%80%908798. The DHI eclipse-temurin-17-jdk packages for Alpine 3.23 ship Bouncy Castle FIPS in their eclipse-temurin-17-jdk-fips subpackage, as /usr/lib/bouncycastle/bc-fips-<version>.jar. Read the manifest of every jar in every published eclipse-temurin-17-jdk-fips package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine security repository (18 versions, 17.0.18.8-r0 to 17.0.21.9.1.2-r0; x86_64, and aarch64 for 17.0.18.8-r0 to 17.0.19.10-r6). The bc-fips jar is 2.1.2 in 17.0.18.8-r0 to 17.0.20.1.1-r0 and in 17.0.20.8-r0 and 17.0.20.8-r1, and 2.1.3 in 17.0.20.1.1-r1, and in 17.0.20.8.1.1-r2 and every later build. The bc-fips jar in every one of these builds contains the NativeEntropySource class. 17.0.20.8-r0 sorts after 17.0.20.1.1-r1 but went back to bc-fips 2.1.2, so the range closes at 17.0.20.1.1-r1, reopens at 17.0.20.8-r0 and closes again at 17.0.20.8.1.1-r2, the next build with 2.1.3. None of the eclipse-temurin-17-jdk, eclipse-temurin-17-jdk-oci-config or eclipse-temurin-17-jdk-fips-oci-config packages published for Alpine 3.23 contains a Bouncy Castle jar.

Upstream lists only x86 and x86-64 with the native library in use as affected, so aarch64 builds do not run this code, but the range below covers the owner as a whole. The DHI eclipse-temurin-8-jdk packages for Alpine 3.23 ship Bouncy Castle FIPS in their eclipse-temurin-8-jdk-fips subpackage, as /usr/lib/bouncycastle/bc-fips-<version>.jar, byte-identical to the Maven Central bc-fips jar of that version. Read the bc-fips jar manifest in every published eclipse-temurin-8-jdk-fips package for Alpine 3.23 (x86_64: 16 versions, 8.482.08-r0 to 8.512.09-r1; aarch64: 8 versions, 8.482.08-r0 to 8.492.09-r6); each download matched the repository index checksum. bc-fips is 2.1.2 in 8.482.08-r0 to 8.504.01-r0 and 2.1.3 in 8.504.01-r1 and every later build. The range ends at 8.504.01-r1, the first build with bc-fips 2.1.3.
